classification.difficultyReason: Interpret cumulative counts, explain successive differences and complete the partly supplied frequency table.

spec.description: One shared cumulative histogram. Source cyan fill and teal outlines do not distinguish data series; the native version uses unfilled bars with black outlines.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent shared histogram; no ogive or response values are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Identify the total number of scores.

answer.worked: The final cumulative frequency is $14$, so there are $14$ scores.
The first cumulative frequency is $5$, so $5$ observations have score $42$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why the frequency of 43 is 5.

answer.short: Subtract the cumulative frequency at $42$ from that at $43$: $10-5=5$.
answer.worked:
The cumulative counts include all scores up to the stated score. Their difference counts only the observations with score $43$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Frequency of }43&=10-5\\\text{Frequency of }43&=5\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Complete the frequency table from the histogram.

answer.worked:
For scores $42,43,44,45,46$, the bar heights give cumulative frequencies $5,10,12,12,14$.

Subtract successive cumulative frequencies to obtain the missing frequencies:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Frequency of }44&=12-10\\\text{Frequency of }44&=2\\\text{Frequency of }45&=12-12\\\text{Frequency of }45&=0\\\text{Frequency of }46&=14-12\\\text{Frequency of }46&=2\end{align*}$$

The completed frequencies are $5,5,2,0,2$. Their sum is $14$, agreeing with the final cumulative frequency.
